Abbotsford is a single city in the Fraser Valley Regional District, and this page covers the whole city rather than one neighbourhood, so a townhome's own street matters more than a sub-area label.
The hospital anchor for the city is at 32900 Marshall Road, Abbotsford, which helps buyers place central complexes against daily health trips.
The City states it adopted a new Official Community Plan (OCP) in December 2025 after more than two years of planning.

The City's own housing update says the December 2025 OCP emphasized more apartments, townhouses and small-scale multi-unit housing (SSMUH) in priority areas, which is the supply context for new townhome product in Abbotsford.
The City states the housing units enabled by the OCP satisfy its 2024 Interim Housing Needs Report target of 37,185 units in the next 20 years.

blocks.text: Abbotsford 55+ Townhomes: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Abbotsford adopted Zoning Bylaw amendments in June 2024 to implement provincial small-scale multi-unit housing and Transit-Oriented Areas legislation, as the City states in its housing update.

A strata rental-restriction bylaw cannot be relied on in any Abbotsford 55+ townhome, because the Province states all strata rental-restriction bylaws became invalid on November 24, 2022, while short-term rental bylaws are still allowed.

blocks.text: Abbotsford 55+ Townhomes: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Abbotsford water and sewer bills are billed bi-monthly for most customers, and the City states properties not connected to City water or sewer are not charged for those services.

Starting in January 2027, solid waste fees move onto the Abbotsford utility bill alongside water and sewer, and will no longer appear on the annual Property Tax Notice, except the $5 solid waste charge for strata units which stays on the tax notice.
The City was approved for up to $25.6 million in federal Housing Accelerator Fund funding, and states all of its Housing Accelerator Fund initiatives are complete.
Hospital parking is paid, with a day rate of $8.25 and a one-month permit at $65.75 on the Fraser Health page, alongside the lower seniors permit rates.
Abbotsford's Tax Rates Bylaw, 2025 is Bylaw No. 3643-2025, and its rates are expressed per $1,000 of taxable value.
BC Transit runs the Central Fraser Valley system that serves Abbotsford, and its regional page is the operator source for routes, fares and rider information for this city.

handyDART in the Central Fraser Valley is an accessible, door-to-door service for people with permanent or temporary disabilities that prevent them using fixed-route transit without assistance, as BC Transit states.

blocks.text: Abbotsford 55+ Townhomes: risks and due diligence

items.t: The biggest due diligence risk in a 55+ townhome is trusting a listing label instead of the filed bylaws, because new and changed bylaws do not take effect until filed at the Land Title Office, with the pet-bylaw exception the Province notes.

faq.a: The 55-plus index lists 2626 Countess St as a 55+ gated townhouse complex, but an index entry is not a bylaw. Ask the seller for the current bylaws filed at the Land Title Office and the Form B, and check whether the age bylaw, pet rule and rental wording in those documents match the listing.

faq.q: Can my 52-year-old partner live with me in a 55+ townhome?
faq.a: Yes, if you are the specified resident, the Province requires an exemption for your younger spouse or partner. A specified resident meets the age requirement or holds a legacy exemption, and the family exemptions added on May 1, 2023 cover younger spouses or partners and defined children cases. The complex can also add its own further exemptions in its bylaws, so read both the provincial rule and the filed bylaws.

faq.q: Can I rent out a 55+ townhome I buy in Abbotsford?
faq.a: A strata cannot ban long-term renting through a rental-restriction bylaw, because the Province states no strata corporation may have a residential rental-restriction bylaw after November 24, 2022. The tenant still has to satisfy the 55+ age bylaw or an exemption, because the age bylaw governs who may reside.

faq.q: How close is hospital care for a 55+ buyer?
faq.a: That does not measure distance from any one complex, so a buyer should map the specific townhome address to Marshall Road themselves. Fraser Health also lists seniors parking permits at that hospital, at $18.75 for one week and $51.75 for one month.
